title: I Let Meta Muse Talk to Customer Service Bots. It Didn’t Go Well
key_facts: A CNET reviewer, a customer of Visible (Verizon's cheap all-digital phone brand, $25 a month), keeps getting spam calls and messages meant for a man named Andrew, probably the number's previous owner.
The reviewer asked Meta's Muse, a personal AI agent app, to talk to Visible's chatbot and check who is formally listed as owner of the number.
Visible blocks bot visits, so Muse could not get through; it also got blocked in a guest chat and the reviewer hit a 403 forbidden error after taking over the browser.
Muse found a data-broker page linking the number to Andrew and advised requesting removal from sites such as WhitePages and FastBackgroundCheck.
The reviewer was escalated to Visible's advanced support, which said to keep the browser open for 4 to 24 hours.
The reviewer concludes most websites block bots, so Muse still feels like a regular chatbot giving guidance to follow.
The problem was not solved at the time of writing.
quote_evidence: But Muse couldn’t get through, as Visible blocks bot visits.
But with a lot of these websites blocking AI agents, it makes autonomous task completion a challenge.
For me, in this situation, Muse still feels like a regular chatbot, giving guidance for me to follow.
why_it_matters_hint: Websites that block bots limit how much AI agents can finish on their own.
notes: First-hand test by one CNET reviewer (name not in the text). Visible's own response was not sought. CNET affiliate boilerplate skipped.
